nodes.description: Complex IV deficiency also injures the putamen and periaqueductal grey — the lesion distribution of Leigh syndrome — but in CMT4K this appears years after the presenting polyneuropathy rather than as the initial event. This node is the mechanistic bridge between CMT4K and SURF1-related Leigh syndrome, and why the two are the same molecular defect with different tempo.

evidence.reference_title: SURF1 deficiency causes demyelinating Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: Two patients had brain MRI abnormalities, including putaminal and periaqueductal lesions, and developed cerebellar ataxia years after polyneuropathy.

nodes.description: Biallelic SURF1 variants abolish the SURF1 assembly factor for cytochrome c oxidase. The index splice-site variant produced no normally spliced transcript and no SURF1 protein. Critically, complex IV activity was only partially reduced in muscle and fibroblasts rather than abolished.

evidence.reference_title: SURF1 deficiency causes demyelinating Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: The c.107-2A>G mutation produced no normally spliced transcript, leading to SURF1 absence. However, complex IV remained partially functional in muscle and fibroblasts.

evidence.reference_title: Tissue- and species-specific differences in cytochrome c oxidase assembly induced by SURF1 defects.
evidence.snippet: The crucial differences observed are an accumulation of abundant COX1 assembly intermediates, low content of COX monomer and preferential recruitment of COX into I-III2-IVn SCs in SURF1 patient fibroblasts

nodes.description: Energy failure in myelinating Schwann cells produces severe demyelination with motor nerve conduction velocities below 25 m/s. The specific step by which reduced complex IV capacity injures the myelinating Schwann cell has not been demonstrated directly in this disease.
nodes.id: Schwann Cell Energy Failure and Demyelination

evidence.reference_title: SURF1 deficiency causes demyelinating Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease.
evidence.snippet: All 3 patients with SURF1-associated CMT4 presented with severe childhood-onset neuropathy, motor nerve conduction velocities <25 m/s, and lactic acidosis.

evidence.reference_title: SURF1 deficiency: a multi-centre natural history study.
evidence.snippet: Peripheral neuropathy was present in 13/16 (81%) (demyelinating 7/16, axonal 2/16).

nodes.description: The defining clinical presentation: severe demyelinating polyneuropathy beginning in childhood, which may be followed years later by central nervous system involvement.
